content: Halcinonide is a topical medication prescribed to alleviate symptoms such as itching, redness, dryness, crusting, scaling, inflammation, and discomfort associated with various skin conditions. It may also be prescribed for other uses, so consult your doctor or pharmacist for additional information. Halcinonide is available in ointment, cream, and liquid forms, with varying strengths, and is intended for application to the skin. Typically, it is applied two or three times daily. Follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully, and consult your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Use halcinonide exactly as directed. Do not use more or less of the medication, or apply it more frequently than prescribed. Avoid applying it to areas of the body not specified by your doctor, and do not wrap or bandage the treated area unless instructed to do so. Before applying the medication, thoroughly wash or soak the affected area unless doing so causes irritation. Apply a thin layer of the ointment, cream, or liquid to the affected area and rub it in gently. If using the liquid on your scalp, part your hair, apply a small amount to the affected area, and rub it in gently. Allow the liquid to dry before washing or rubbing the area. You may wash your hair as usual, but avoid doing so immediately after applying the medication. Avoid prolonged use of halcinonide on the face, genital or rectal areas, skin creases, or armpits unless directed by your doctor. If using halcinonide on a child’s diaper area, avoid tight-fitting diapers or plastic pants, as these may increase the risk of side effects. Do not apply cosmetics or other skin products to the treated area without consulting your doctor. If your doctor instructs you to wrap or bandage the treated area, follow these steps: 1. Wash or soak the area thoroughly. 2. While the skin is still moist, gently rub the medication into the affected area. 3. Cover the area with plastic wrap (e.g., Saran Wrap or Handi-Wrap). Secure the plastic with gauze, an elastic bandage, or adhesive tape on the normal skin surrounding the treated area. Alternatively, plastic gloves, plastic bags, or a shower cap may be used for hands, feet, or the scalp, respectively. 4. If the area is moist, leave the edges partially unsealed or puncture the wrap to allow excess moisture to escape. 5. Leave the plastic wrap in place for the duration specified by your doctor, typically no longer than 12 hours per day. 6. Cleanse the skin and reapply the medication each time a new plastic wrap is applied. Notify your doctor if the treated area worsens or if you experience burning, swelling, redness, or oozing of pus. Do not stop using the medication abruptly without consulting your doctor. Before using halcinonide, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to halcinonide or any other medications. Provide a list of all prescription and nonprescription medications you are taking, including cancer chemotherapy agents, other topical medications, and vitamins. Inform your doctor if you have an infection or a history of diabetes, glaucoma, cataracts, circulation disorders, or immune system disorders. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, notify your doctor. If you become pregnant while using halcinonide, contact your doctor immediately. If you miss a dose, apply it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not apply a double dose to compensate for a missed one. Halcinonide may cause side effects. Notify your doctor if you experience any of the following minor side effects, especially if they are severe or persistent: Drying or cracking of the skin Acne Itching Burning Changes in skin color If you experience any of the following severe side effects, contact your doctor immediately: Severe skin rash Difficulty breathing or swallowing Wheezing Signs of a skin infection, such as redness, swelling, or oozing pus Serious side effects can be reported to the FDA’s MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program online or by phone. Store halcinonide in its original container, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excessive heat, and do not allow it to freeze. Dispose of any expired or unused medication properly, and do not use it to treat other skin conditions. Consult your pharmacist for guidance on proper disposal. Keep all appointments with your doctor while using this medication. Do not share halcinonide with others. If you have questions about refilling your prescription, consult your pharmacist. Halcinonide is sold under the brand names Halog® and Halog®-E.
